as_told.title: Lightning-scarred stone on Oshidto Ishi Hill

plain: Stones on Oshidoishi Hill in Japan are said to have been struck by lightning again and again, and researchers from Kumamoto University are said to have seen it happen several times. A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm tells this on the show. He says the Kumamoto team "actually witnessed these things being struck by lightning on multiple occasions." When he describes the stone itself, he says "the scarring pock marks and melted top of this stone are a result of lightning strikes," and he does not mention the university witnesses there. If true, the marks on the stones would come from lightning, not from tools or weather.
